current: Define chay, thuần chay and suitable-for-vegetarians claims by reference to TCVN 13625 in the Food Safety Law's implementing rules, and make meat-free claims enforceable
proposed: TCVN 13625:2023 already defines vegetarian and vegan claims but allows egg, milk and honey in vegetarian and says nothing on alliums; false chay claims are already unlawful under the goods-label rules. Ask MOH or VFA to state that an unqualified chay or thuần chay claim means the TCVN 13625 vegan criteria, that egg or milk must be named in a qualifier, and that allium-free stays voluntary; pair with DMV-07 testing.

current: Require honest percentage labelling of blended (hybrid) meat products
proposed: Largely in force: any ingredient named in the product name must be quantified (Decree 43/2017 Art 13(4), carried into Decree 37/2026); Vissan prints the named meat on 28 of 29 meat-named formulations. Narrow to generic names (giò lụa, xúc xích, hotdog) through a voluntary industry code stating the meat share when a plant or fungal protein replaces 10% or more of the meat.

current: Honest percentage labelling; value lines first; no imitation claims
proposed: Add: No national standard sets a minimum meat content (TCVN 7049:2020, 7050:2020, 7048:2020), so a 20 to 30% extender keeps the meat product name. The meat must be quantified if the name names it; Vissan already sells meat-named products at 27 to 65% named lean. A 55% lean sausage with 20 to 30% of lean replaced keeps 38.5 to 44% (our calculation).

Protein claim conditions are in TCVN 14429:2025 (voluntary, Codex): source at 5 g and high (cao) at 10 g per 100 g, or 2.5 g and 5 g per 100 kcal. Print 10 g đạm/100 g on the front because the per 100 kcal route lets watery foods claim high at 4 to 5 g per 100 g. Avoid function claims (no approval route). The claim needs no registration or advertising approval.

where: ch24.2 The GMO collision; ch24.6 item 2
current: If purified precision-fermented proteins must be declared as products of a GMO, their most likely Vietnamese buyers face a clash with their own brand promise
proposed: The mandatory GMO label applies only when a GM ingredient exceeds 5% of total ingredients and not when neither the gene nor its product is detectable (Decree 15/2018 Art 10; Joint Circular 45/2015 Art 1). Lactoferrin is used at about 0.08% (80 mg per 100 g in a VitaDairy formula), so the clash is with voluntary non-GMO claims and with high-inclusion uses, not with lactoferrin-type ingredients.
